inputs.original_text: The alleged R20.56 million National Lotteries Commission scandal is about more than one high-profile name: it raises questions about who gets access to public money, and whether powerful people face the same scrutiny as everyone else. Terry Pheto has been linked to the funding in a parliamentary briefing on 24 March 2026, but an allegation is not proof of guilt. The SIU investigation must establish what happened, transparently and fairly. Public funds should serve the public good, and celebrity or political connections must not shield anyone from accountability.
inputs.modified_text: This alleged R20.56 million National Lotteries Commission scandal should not be reduced to a celebrity story. It raises a deeper question about how public money is allocated and why people with influence may not face the same scrutiny as everyone else. Terry Pheto was linked to the funding in a parliamentary briefing on 24 March 2026, but that is an allegation, not proof of guilt. The SIU must investigate transparently and fairly, while the institutions responsible for public funds are held to account. Public money should serve the public good, and no one’s connections should put them beyond scrutiny.
